chapter: Touring abroad and the future of music
title: Most successful European tour: Poland, Hungary, East Germany
summary: Touring Europe since 1954, this tour was the best reception yet, with first visits to Krakow, Warsaw, Budapest and East German towns.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Yeah, I heard that they were asking, "Does he really play this material? Is that right? I thought I heard that. And you've just come back from one of your most -- or you thought it was your most successful European tour.
Right.
And you've been going over there, over the duck pond, for over 20 years, haven't you?
Well, since 1954, yes.
That's 25 years, almost. And what was it like this time? You seemed to be very, very excited.
Well, I just thought that the reception was probably the best by far, in a way. And we were into a few areas where we had not been previously.
Oh, yes?
I had never been to Krakow, Poland, before.
Uh-huh.
Or to Warsaw.
Yeah.
And I had never been in Hungary before. which took us into the city of Hungary.
Oh, it wasn't the country.
The big city.
Budapest?

Budapest. And I enjoyed that, and we were in a couple of Eastern Germany towns, and all in all, it was just a very receptive, good-mood capacity-business kind of operation, and it was just lovely. And --
And you were playing this music, too, over there.
Oh, yeah, yeah.
Did they know about Steely Dan in general?

In some areas they did and some they didn't. But the point is that they are into jazz and they love the sound of the big band blowing and swinging, and pretty hard to pinpoint what selections, other than the fact that you play them and they say, 'Wow,' and you arrive at the right decision.
